look-alike cans by RGB label, never by SAM3 brand-noun prompt](global/sam3-brand-noun-can-collision.md) \\u2014 two or more similar cans/cylinders are present and the task names one by brand (\\\"tomato sauce\\\", \\\"alphabet soup\\\", a soup can)\\n- [Re-issue a pick with a nearby landmark when generic picking makes only contact.](global/spatial-qualified-repick.md) \\u2014 A generic Pi0 pick contacts the target object but leaves it upright or ungrasped, and a distinctive nearby landmark is visible in the scene.\\n- [Support an elongated held object on the destination floor before chaining yaw and pitch rotations](global/support-assisted-axis-reorientation.md) \\u2014 an elongated held object must be reoriented inside a shallow container and airborne wrist rotations slip, drift, or exceed the reachable workspace\\n- [Translate a weak hooked grasp with surface support before lifting over thresholds.](global/support-guided-weak-hook-translation.md) \\u2014 A narrow rim or handle hook survives gentle motion but slips under airborne rotation or long carry.\\n- [Re-check duplicate identity before tuning a non-firing placement.](global/verify-duplicate-semantics.md) \\u2014 A task has duplicate objects and repeated visually plausible placements do not trigger the predicate\\n- [Trust visual grasp evidence over the Pi0 pick success flag.](global/visual-over-pick-heuristic.md) \\u2014 A pi0_pick reports success false but the object is visibly moved or held and gripper/image evidence contradicts the heuristic\\n\\n## {
  "path": "workspace/vla_baselines/cache/harness-assets-download/memory/7db66088d06d04ae097682332a09704f13e6fc0c/GPT_5.5_xhigh/global/moka-pot-grasp-the-handle-not-the-body.md",
  "size": 2430,
  "content": "---\nid: moka-pot-grasp-the-handle-not-the-body\nscope: global\nkind: strategy\ntitle: Grasp a moka pot by its thin side handle, not its wide body or cap\napplies_when: picking a moka pot (or any wide low-poly pot/kettle with a slim handle)\n  when top-down body grasps stall and Pi0 will not close\nsymptom:\n- moka pot\n- pi0 never closes\n- gripper opening 0.078\n- descent stalls on shoulder\n- cap grasp slips\n- wide body grasp\nevidence:\n  cells:\n  - 10_task_t8_s0\n  attempts: 3\n  solved_seeds:\n  - 0\nconfidence: single-shot\nrelated: []\n---\n\nA moka pot is reliably grasped top-down by its thin side HANDLE; its wide octagonal body and thin cap knob are both un-graspable and Pi0 refuses to close on it.\n\n**Why:** The pot's upper chamber/shoulder is ~7.8cm across \u2014 essentially the gripper's full open span (~8cm) \u2014 so open fingers collide with the shoulder and the OSC descent stalls before the fingers can straddle the body; the only narrow top-down feature (the cap knob, ~1cm) gives a gap-0.012 pinch that slips. The handle is a slim (~1.5-2cm) rigid tube offset laterally from the body, so fingers descend around it without shoulder collision and close to a firm gap ~0.020. Pi0 (pi0_pick) descended but never issued a close command on this pot in 3/3 tries \u2014 its trained distribution does not commit to this geometry.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- Localize the handle's top-of-curve segment (back_project pixels). Note the tube axis; rotate the\n  wrist yaw ~90deg so the fingers close ACROSS the tube (not along it). A 90deg rotate_wrist drifts\n  the eef ~0.1-0.15m \u2014 re-center over the handle before descending.\n- Descend to tube level (~z where finger tips meet the tube), set_gripper +1. Confirm gap ~0.016-0.024\n  (tube) \u2014 NOT ~0.012 (cap, slips) and NOT ~0.078 (blocked open, no grip). Lift and confirm the pot\n  hangs upright by the handle.\n- To place: the body hangs offset from the grip (here ~+0.038 x, +0.067 y; measure per pick, it can\n  swing). Aim eef xy = destination_center - body_offset, descend until the base rests, release.\n- Do NOT waste attempts on pi0_pick or on top-down body/cap grasps for this object class.\n\n**Falsify:** If a future scene has a moka pot whose upper chamber is clearly narrower than the gripper\nspan and pi0_pick closes and lifts it, or a top-down body grasp seats and lifts it, then the body/Pi0\nroute is viable there and this lesson is over-general.\n\n**Related:** [[task-family_libero10_task_t8]]\n"
}

{
  "path": "workspace/vla_baselines/cache/harness-assets-download/memory/7db66088d06d04ae097682332a09704f13e6fc0c/GPT_5.5_xhigh/global/contact-skill-state-change.md",
  "size": 1461,
  "content": "---\nid: contact-skill-state-change\nscope: global\nkind: strategy\ntitle: Use Pi0 pick as a contact skill for fixture state changes.\napplies_when: A task asks to change a fixture state such as turning a stove on or\n  off rather than transporting an object.\nsymptom:\n- no object target\n- stove knob\n- peak_lift_zero\n- contact task\nevidence:\n  cells:\n  - goal_task_t7_s0\n  attempts:\n  - 1\nconfidence: single-shot\nrelated:\n- visual-over-pick-heuristic\n---\n\n\nFor fixture state-change tasks, `pi0_pick` can be repurposed as a closed-loop contact controller by disabling the lift/closure success thresholds and using the task verb as the prompt.\n\n**Why:** Pi0 has a learned visual contact behavior for stove controls; the benchmark predicate is the fixture state, not object lift, so a zero-lift trajectory can still be the correct manipulation.\n**How to apply:** First identify the fixture and contact target in RGB. Then call `pi0_pick` or the equivalent contact wrapper with a short verb prompt such as `turn off the stove`, `max_chunks=16-24`, `lift_thresh=999`, and `gripper_closed_thresh=0`. Judge success from `terminated`, images, and fixture state evidence rather than peak lift.\n**Falsify:** If repeated staged calls reach the control region but never change the fixture state, or if the prompt drives toward a loose object instead of the fixture control, this contact-skill shortcut is not grounded for that scene.\n**Related:** [[visual-over-pick-heuristic]]\n"
}

      "id": "call_00_Mls8evl7IdONpIhTXsud8401",
      "name": "finish",
      "input": {
        "status": "success",
        "summary": "SOLVED in one episode (terminated=true at step 24) on libero_10 task 2, seed 0: \"turn on the stove and put the moka pot on it\".\n\nPhase 1 — stove on: used pi0_pick as a closed-loop CONTACT skill (prompt \"turn the stove knob\", lift_thresh 999, gripper_closed_thresh 0). In 5 chunks it reached the knob at (-0.183, 0.215, 0.938), closed on the lever and rotated it; the hot-plate coil rings turned bright red (stove ON) — confirmed in RGB.\n\nPhase 2 — the hard part, grasping the pot. The pot's handle is a closed loop whose bar sat at z 0.975-1.03 on a 13cm-tall upright pot. Every handle hook (pi0_pick, and scripted move_pose with pitch 0.45/0.9 at yaw 0 and 90) stalled at eef z~1.04-1.055. I calibrated the fingertips from the wrist world map and found the pads sit essentially AT the eef height (eef_z+0.006), so the bar was physically unreachable from above. A diagnostic descent at x=-0.015 and at (0.033, +0.10) then proved the \"wall\" was NOT an IK limit (the eef reached z=0.950 at x=0.033 once clear of the pot) — the pot itself was the obstruction. The pot got knocked onto its side during those attempts, which was lucky: a lying cylinder is an easier target.\n\nPhase 3 — re-localized the tipped pot from scratch (agentview/wrist region + point back_project): axis from base (0.029, 0.074, 0.976) to cap end (-0.044, -0.037, 0.942), diameter 4.2cm at the cap growing to 7.6cm at the base. Derived the correct cross-diameter gripper yaw = 0.99 rad (a first try at 2.154 was 33° off and put a fingertip on the pot's top), descended onto the narrow upper chamber, and closed: the opening settled at a 6.7cm finger gap = exactly the pot's local diameter, with the wrist image showing the pot's white body pressed between both pads. Lifted it clean off the table.\n\nPhase 4 — carried with gripper:+1 on measured held-offsets (pot base 9.2cm from the grip along (0.52, 0.855)) in two sub-0.20m waypoints so the pot's centre landed at (-0.068, 0.191), i.e. 1.8cm from the coil centre (-0.062, 0.208), then lowered it; the goal predicate fired on touchdown at eef z=0.9965, before a release was even required.\n\nAudit and 24-step recipe JSONL written to the episode directory. No reset was used."
      }
    }
  ]
}
